limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.
rule: For each row independently, find the most frequent nonzero colour (the main colour); the output row holds that colour exactly on the cells where the input row did not, and 0 where it did. Noise cells of other colours are discarded.
scope: Supported: sampled width 6..20 and height 2..8; per-row main colour drawn from a shuffled palette (distinct across rows up to 9 rows); row patterns of contiguous run, run with interior gap, alternating parity, or scattered subset; 0..2 noise colours per row placed on cells not holding the main colour, with the main colour strictly outnumbering all noise. Not supported: rows with no main colour (all-zero rows), rows where the main colour fills every cell or none, frequency ties between main and noise colours (the reference breaks such ties by the lower colour value; one canonical row relies on that and is only reproduced via explicit latent arguments), and noise colours equal to the row's main colour.
constraints: Every row has at least one main-colour cell and at least one cell without it, so every row changes.
The main colour count in each row is strictly greater than the count of every other nonzero colour in that row (random path), making the main colour unambiguous.
Noise cells never overlap main-colour cells and never use the row's main colour or 0.
Noise colours are chosen from colours not used as any row's main colour when such colours exist, mirroring the fixtures' separate main/noise palettes.
The output grid never equals the input grid.
known_limitations: Canonical train pair 2 row 1 has a 3-vs-3 tie between colours 4 and 7; the archived reference resolves ties to the lowest colour value. The random generator never samples ties, and validate() reproduces that row only through explicit latent arguments.
Scattered-subset rows may coincidentally resemble run/gap/alternate patterns; this is harmless since the rule is pattern-agnostic.
For heights above 9 main colours repeat across rows (rule is row-local so this remains unambiguous).
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback

checks: Four row-pattern families with controlled noise
Main colour strictly dominates other nonzero colours on random rows
Complement output constructed from latent main-colour positions; canonical tie kept explicit
No archived solver import or file I/O in standalone module
